material_definitions: The lithium argyrodites are explored as solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries.
This study focuses on the influence of aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1	−xGexS5I.
The goal is to design better performing solid electrolytes by inducing anion site disorder and lowering the activation barrier for ionic motion.
Measurements utilized X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance.
The lithium argyrodites are explored as solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries.
This study focuses on the influence of aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1	−xGexS5I.
The goal is to design better performing solid electrolytes by inducing anion site disorder and lowering the activation barrier for ionic motion.
Measurements utilized X-ray and neutron diffraction, impedance spectroscopy, and nuclear magnetic resonance.
The materials studied are lithium argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I, synthesized by substituting Ge4+ for P in Li6PS5I.
This substitution induces site disorder between the S2– and I– positions.
The increasing disorder is correlated to a sharp decrease in the activation barrier and high ionic conductivity.
Measurements were performed on both cold-pressed and sintered samples.

The Li+ superionic argyrodites Li6+xP1-xGexS5I have been synthesized with increasing Ge4+/P5+ ratios.
The series is composed of solid solutions with minor impurity phase fractions of LiI and/or Li4GeS4.
Full solid solutions can be synthesized up to a composition of at least Li6.7P0.3Ge0.7S5I.
Ionic conductivity was measured using impedance spectroscopy on cold-pressed pellets.

Aliovalent substitution in Li6+xP1-xGexS5I argyrodite solid solutions was performed.

Figure 6: Activation barrier and ionic conductivity of  $Li_{6+x}P_{1-x}Ge_xS_5I$  as a function of the refined Ge content, as obtained from impedance spectroscopy. With increasing  $Ge^{4+}$  and  $Li^+$  concentration, the ionic conductivity increases over three orders of magnitude, reaching a conductivity of  $\sigma = 5.4$  mS cm<sup>-1</sup>. An inflection point starting  $\sim 20\%$  Ge can be seen that leads to a strong decrease of the activation barrier.
